note: A2.5. Baseline 2026-09-16 = 0.00 on every row: `HardWorker.perform_async(order.id)` reads no literal and `include Sidekiq::Worker` reads no literal, so BOTH sides collapse to the framework tag `unresolved:sidekiq` and never pair. Ruby names the task nowhere as a string: the identity is the receiver on the producer side and the enclosing class on the consumer side. The paren-less `sidekiq_options queue: 'critical'` additionally names a real broker queue -- both nodes exist for one class, deliberately.

expect_nodes.name: queue_producer:HardWorker
expect_nodes.note: receiver of perform_async, not the order id payload

expect_nodes.name: queue_consumer:critical
expect_nodes.note: the explicitly named Sidekiq queue, read off a paren-less call

expect_edges.note: producer and consumer of one job, paired across two services
